uncertain: The chart does not print a numeric value on the May bar; its exact kWh figure must be inferred from its position relative to the 10,000 gridline (it appears to be well below 10,000, possibly under 2,000–3,000).
No threshold, baseline, or anomaly rule is printed on the chart or in the form fields to define what constitutes 'standard' vs. 'critical' low usage.

The y-axis break symbol indicates the scale is truncated, so the absolute magnitude of May's value relative to zero is visually compressed; the true deviation from a normal range cannot be quantified without external data.
The month order on the x-axis (Apr, Jan, Jun, Feb, Mar, May) is non-chronological, which may affect interpretation of trend or seasonality if assumed.
No legend, annotation, or highlight distinguishes May as an anomaly; the visual outlier status is based solely on bar height comparison.
